articles.title: 💸 Social Giant To Pay $16.68 Billion For Designing Apps To Hook Teenagers; Calls It A 'Rounding Error With Feelings'
articles.dateline: MENLO PARK — reported between two infinite scrolls
paras: A social-media giant agreed to pay up to $16.68 billion to settle claims it deliberately engineered its apps to hook teenagers — a number large enough to sting slightly and small enough to be recouped by roughly Tuesday afternoon.

"We've always prioritized well-being," the company said, of platforms scientifically optimized to be impossible to put down, now paying a historic sum to acknowledge they succeeded. Analysts note the settlement confirms the apps were addictive by design, which everyone already knew — having checked the app in question about four times while reading this very sentence.

articles.title: 🧑‍💻 The Humans Who Trained The A.I. Are Laid Off After 21 Years; The Student Has Officially Fired The Teacher
articles.dateline: THE INTERNET — reported by a suddenly very quiet crowd
paras: A tech giant is shutting down its long-running human-work marketplace after 21 years — the vast crowd of people who labeled the data and answered the questions that taught modern AI how to think — in what may be the most on-the-nose ending in tech history.

"We thank everyone for their contributions," the company said, closing the very service whose workers hand-fed the machine-learning era one tiny task at a time, until the machine no longer needed them. Historians will note that the tutors trained the pupil so well it graduated, took their job, and turned off the lights on the way out.

articles.title: 🔋 A.I. Company's Own Chip Beats The Chip King On Efficiency; The Customer Has Built A Better Toll Booth
articles.dateline: SAN FRANCISCO — reported by the light of one very efficient LED
paras: A leading AI lab says its first custom inference chip now outperforms the dominant chipmaker's flagship systems on AI-work-per-watt — meaning the industry's biggest customer looked at the world's most expensive toll booth and decided to build its own road.

"We needed efficiency at our scale," the company said, of a chip born from the timeless frustration of paying someone else a fortune every single day. Analysts note that when your suppliers get rich enough, they eventually become your competitors — a lesson the chip king is now learning at a very high, very well-cooled clock speed.

articles.title: 🚀 Rocket Company Plans A $100 Billion Launch Complex; The Number Has Left Earth Without A Rocket
articles.dateline: SOUTH TEXAS — reported from a respectful distance
paras: A rocket company unveiled plans for a staggering $100 billion launch complex, a sum so enormous it has achieved escape velocity on its own and no longer requires a vehicle to leave the atmosphere.

"We're building for the future," the company said, of a facility that costs more than the annual budget of several nations and, presumably, comes with genuinely excellent parking. Analysts note that in 2026, the phrase "we're spending $100 billion" is now delivered with the breezy calm most people reserve for "we're getting a new couch."

articles.title: 🤯 A.I. Industry Now Releases A New Model Roughly Every Time You Blink; Nobody, Including The Makers, Can Keep Up
articles.dateline: EVERYWHERE AT ONCE — reported before this model was outdated
paras: Trackers now count more than 362 AI model releases across major labs this year, a torrent so relentless that by the time you finish reading about a new state-of-the-art model, it has been quietly superseded by two others and a weekend hackathon.

"Innovation is accelerating," companies insist, of a release schedule that has turned staying current into a full-time job with no salary and no end. Experts recommend simply picking one model, loving it, and refusing to look at the news — the way one survives any stampede: by standing very still and closing your eyes.

horoscopes.text: You will check an app four times while trying to stop checking it. This is not your fault. It's a legal settlement.
Do not chase every new model today. Pick one. Love it. Close the other tabs. There, at last, is peace.
Mercury reaches escape velocity on budget alone. Aim high, spend wildly, and park with tremendous ease.

tech_tip: If keeping up with new A.I. models feels impossible, that's because it is. Pick one, learn it well, and let the stampede pass.
gadget_watch: No new gadget this week — just a $100 billion launch complex and a chip war where the customers now build better chips than their supplier. The takeaway: everything is enormous, and your phone is fine, actually.
